description: A coordinator asks every participant to prepare and then commit; participants hold locks and block while the decision is unknown.
A business transaction split into local transactions, one per service, each with a compensating action run in reverse order on failure.
A new operation that semantically cancels a committed step, such as a refund for a charge, rather than a database rollback.
An orchestrator calls each step and decides what runs next; in choreography each service reacts to events and publishes its own.
Writing to the database and then to a broker as two operations: a crash in between leaves them inconsistent.
The event is inserted into an outbox table in the same local transaction as the change, and a relay publishes it at least once.
Reading a database's write-ahead log or binlog to emit every committed change as an event, as Debezium does.
A client-generated id sent with a request so the server returns the stored result for a retry instead of repeating the operation.
